correctness.rationale: The exact \(\mathrm{Beta}(1,b)\) survival function reduces the probability inequality to \(f_b(t)\ge0\). The derivative has at most two critical points, so the global sign reduces to the unique interior minimum for \(b>2\). The minimum value \(H(b)\) is strictly decreasing by an envelope derivative, positive at \(b=2\) and tends to minus infinity, proving a unique sharp threshold. The explicit violating deviation above threshold is exactly the minimizing critical point.

originality.rationale: The closest beta concentration papers address MGF proxy variance, Bernstein-type bounds, or matching-order tail rates. The new statement instead gives an exact if-and-only-if parameter threshold for a one-sided probability inequality with the true variance. Targeted statement searches and the inspected sources did not reveal this threshold or an implication that supplies it.
residual_risks: An equivalent one-sided threshold could exist under different terminology or in literature not surfaced by the targeted searches.

value.rationale: The claim gives a natural complete phase classification inside a canonical skew-beta family for the precise question of when the true variance alone controls an exact Gaussian right tail. It clarifies a substantive distinction between MGF strict sub-Gaussianity and one-sided probability concentration and pinpoints when the Bernstein correction motivated by the beta concentration literature becomes genuinely necessary at the level of the exact tail.
